key_insight: AI-assisted grain-boundary sampling reveals how SrTiO₃ composition and atomic reconstruction control electronic states, electric fields, and local polarization.
engineering_relevance: Controlling grain-boundary stoichiometry and structure offers a route to tuning carrier localization and interfacial electronic behavior in functional perovskites.
method: Combine grand canonical Monte Carlo with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential to sample structures and compositions.
Map chemical-potential stability and compare structural motifs across three grain-boundary geometries.
Use density functional theory and electrostatics analysis to characterize electronic states, fields, and polarization.
evidence_signal: The Σ5(310)[001] phase diagram identifies ten stable structures in four motif families, while DFT reveals four electronic regimes: localized electron-doped, delocalized electron-doped, insulating, and hole-attracting.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational predictions without experimental validation; broader transferability across grain-boundary geometries remains to be established.
paper_title: Uncovering the Structural, Electronic, and Electrostatic Landscapes of SrTiO$_3$ Grain Boundaries via Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
